rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4 and Figs 9-10 - the authors develop a soil-water-balance/stochastic model generating hydrant and upstream demand hydrographs and compare simulated with Venturimeter-measured daily volumes (1990-1999) and hourly discharges (10-day peak period of 1999) at district 10 of the Sinistra Ofanto scheme, Southern Italy.
rows.notes: The study reports no result of its own on the investment cost of on-demand networks nor on supply being guaranteed during peak periods. It only develops and calibrates a model that generates peak-period demand hydrographs for an on-demand pressurised network (daily volumes fit well; hourly simulated peaks sometimes exceed measured ones because network hydraulic constraints are not modelled). The introduction's statements about on-demand systems requiring adequate design for peak-period discharge are general background, not own findings. Demand hydrograph generation is at most an input (precondition) to network design and hence to investment cost, so upstream is set to true.

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is a modelling study (simulated vs measured demand hydrographs) with no cost or supply-reliability analysis; the review passage attributes to it a claim about investment cost that the study does not address.
